name: Josiah
overview: Josiah was a male king of Judah, recognized as the prophesied son of the house of David and the son of Amon. He is noted for doing right in the sight of the LORD, demonstrating faithful leadership during his reign. His kingship and godly character are significant within the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Josiah means 'let or may YHWH give,' indicating a divine blessing in his identity. He is also referred to by the titles King Josiah and King of Judah, reflecting his royal role and authority over the kingdom of Judah.
familyAndRelationships: Josiah was a descendant of David and the son of Amon and Jedidah. The records also infer connections to Jehoahaz, Eliakim, Mattaniah, and Shallum as fathers, indicating a royal lineage. These relationships establish his place within the Davidic line and the royal family of Judah.
scriptureSignificance: Josiah is important in Scripture as a king who faithfully followed God, leading a significant reformation in Judah. His discovery of the Book of the Law during temple repairs prompted sincere repentance and covenant renewal, highlighting the transformative power of God's Word. His reign is marked by the destruction of idolatry and a delay in Judah's judgment, underscoring his role as a godly reformer.
